(1) the spectral dynamics of single emitters in a broadened ensemble can be extracted from the intensity correlations among the ensemble emission spectra; and (2) spectral correlations can be observed with a pair of avalanche photodetectors at the output of a scanning Michleson interferometer, which provides the required temporal and spectral resolution to overcome ensemble and temporal in-homogeneous broadening.
the spectral dynamics of a single emitter can be extracted from the intensity correlations of an ensemble spectrum, even under broadband illumination.
we show how spectral correlations in a broadband emission spectrum can be used to extract single emitter linewidths from an ensemble spectrum.
